title: Magic of Kitaev spin liquids
authors: Eleonora Lamma, Tim Bauer, Marcello Dalmonte, Mario Collura
abstract: Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are long-range entangled phases of matter and a natural setting for exploring how quantum correlations generate quantum complexity. Motivated by the emergence of magic, or nonstabilizerness, as a diagnostic of many-body complexity beyond entanglement, we study magic of QSLs by computing the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) of the Kitaev honeycomb model. We derive a correspondence between Pauli strings and products of itinerant Majorana operators in the model's free-fermion description; this enables the sampling of SRE using an optimized algorithm for Gaussian states in systems with thousands of spins. Our results show that magic is largest in the gapless phase, where subleading volume-law corrections indicate nonlocal contributions, while in the gapped phases, SRE decreases in quantitative agreement with a perturbative expansion that we develop in the anisotropic limit. At the topological phase transition, SRE exhibits universal scaling dictated by critical exponents.
summary: This work analyzes the Kitaev honeycomb model to quantify quantum complexity using the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), or 'magic.' By calculating SRE across the model's phase diagram, the authors demonstrate that this measure peaks in the gapless QSL phase and provides universal scaling information at the topological phase transition.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum complexity in Quantum Spin Liquids (QSLs) by studying a diagnostic measure called 'magic' or nonstabilizerness, which goes beyond standard entanglement measures.
main_result: Magic is found to be largest in the gapless phase of the Kitaev model, decreases in gapped phases, and exhibits universal scaling at the topological phase transition.
method: The authors compute the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) by mapping Pauli strings to itinerant Majorana operators in the model's free-fermion description, enabling sampling via optimized algorithms for Gaussian states.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Kitaev honeycomb model (KHM) on the honeycomb lattice, which realizes QSLs and is characterized by three bond types ($x, y, z$). The model is analyzed across its phase diagram, including gapless and gapped topological phases.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) and its density ($m_n$), which quantifies 'magic' or nonstabilizerness.
important_parameters: The ratio of coupling constants ($J_x, J_y, J_z$), the system size ($N$ or $L$), and the proximity to the gapless/gapped phase boundaries.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the free-fermion description of the KHM and adapting an existing sampling algorithm for fermionic Gaussian states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SRE across the phase diagram, showing the peak in the gapless phase and the scaling behavior at the critical point.
paper_structure: The paper systematically studies SRE across the entire phase diagram of the KHM, deriving the mathematical correspondence between Pauli strings and Majorana operators, and analyzing the results in the gapless, gapped, and critical regimes.
why_interesting: The use of 'magic' as a complexity measure provides a novel tool to probe the structure of quantum correlations in strongly correlated magnetic systems, complementing standard entanglement measures.
